purpose: Add current primary Irish judgments located in the latest case-law research pass and map their precise evidential limits.

new_authorities.case: Planetwhite Ltd v Hogan & Anor [2025] IEHC 378
new_authorities.relevance: Section 31 applied to a registered owner seeking possession; judgment distinguishes conclusive registered title from evidence of the terms of an underlying transfer.

linked_authorities.relevance: Section 31 does not make the register conclusive evidence of the terms of an underlying transfer or assignment.
Discussed the registered register as an 'iron curtain' and the curative effect of registration.

verified_interpretive_points: Planetwhite states that s.31 applies to a registered owner seeking possession even though that owner was not in possession.
The judgment distinguishes a registered owner's title from the evidential question of the detailed terms of an underlying transfer or assignment.
Section 72(1)(j) does not create a legal right of occupation merely because a person is physically occupying registered land; an existing legal right must be established.
A registered-title proposition must still be analysed alongside overriding interests, burdens and the specific pleadings/evidence in a dispute.
case_law_limits: Planetwhite is a High Court judgment and does not replace Court of Appeal or Supreme Court authority.
Its possession facts are specific and must not be generalized to every occupier dispute.
The judgment does not complete the separate registry-map/physical-boundary case-law search.
No individual property conclusion is drawn.
publication_effect: Strengthens PROP-PROPERTY-TITLE-001 case-law support but does not by itself move any proposition to publication-ready.
